# Vendored: SynthID-text scoring core

This directory is **not our code**. It is copied, unmodified, from
[`systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-token-tell`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-token-tell)
(MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Paul Clark — see `LICENSE.upstream`), at commit
`ed27b531a26780d1050e0dd00d6e566da63b1515`.

## What it is

A TypeScript port of the SynthID-text keyed g-value construction from
[`google-deepmind/synthid-text`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/synthid-text) at commit
`addb4a1`: the 64-bit linear congruential hash seeded from a SHA-256 initialization vector
over the key list, twelve re-hash rounds per g-value, repeated-context and EOS masking, the
mean g-value statistic, and the closed-form Binomial null. It also carries a GPT-2 tokenizer
rebuilt from the merge list, and the pinned generation record the fixtures derive from.

## Why it is vendored rather than installed

There is no published library for SynthID-text detection in JavaScript. The upstream project
is a teaching demo, not a package: its scoring core is cleanly separated from its UI, but it
has no entry point to depend on. Copying the core and leaving its tests intact was the
shortest path to a real detector.

## Why the tests were left unmodified

`watermark/*.test.ts` and `tokenizer/gpt2.test.ts` are upstream's, and they are differential:
their expectations for the hash, the g-values, the masks, and the scores were generated by the
Python reference implementation, not by the TypeScript under test. They are the evidence that
this port reproduces the reference, so editing them would defeat their purpose. The only change
made to this directory was moving the pinned data under `data/pinned/` to match the layout
those tests import from.

Everything under `../src/` is ours, and it is where the evidence-shaped decisions live —
thresholds, minimum sample size, and the limitations attached to each result. The intent is
that the whole of this directory can be replaced by a real library, or by a stricter Bayesian
detector, without touching `../src/detector.ts` beyond its scoring call.

## What it does not do

- It implements the **mean g-value** statistic, not the learned Bayesian detector that both
  the paper and the reference repository use for their headline results. It is weaker.
- Its keys are the **published demonstration keys**. It cannot detect any production
  deployment, whose keys are secret.
- Its hash is a linear congruential generator. Upstream of everything here, the reference
  repository states that it "does not provide any guarantees of cryptographic security".
